newsitem.title: CHINA: American Dream theme park opens in Shanghai suburb.
newsitem.headline: American Dream theme park opens in Shanghai suburb.

text.p: An international consortium of investors opened a $100-million American Dream park on Monday in a Shanghai suburb, the first of five they plan to build in China to cash in on the country's leisure revolution.
But with entrance tickets priced at 100 yuan ($12) for an adult, some residents felt it was too expensive.

The park, on 33.35 hectares (82.4 acre) 26 km (16 miles) northwest of the city centre, offers stunt men, jousting, cowboys and a Miami Vice police show as well as a roller coaster, paddle boats and cartoon characters.

"Two years ago we embarked on our mission of building five parks in strategic locations in China and will realise our dream in the next two to three years," Stephen Hong, chairman of the American Dream Park group, told the opening ceremony.
"Our goal is to make the park a leader in the Chinese entertainment industry," he said.
The American Dream Park group consists of investors from the United States, Hong Kong and Taiwan.
The second park, in the southern city of Guangzhou, is due to open in early 1997 and the others will be built in Wuhan, Beijing and Chengdu.

The park aims to attract three million visitors a year, with a daily capacity of 30,000. The target market is Chinese residents in and visitors to Shanghai, who are expected to stay in the park for an average of six hours, officials said.
They said it was one of the first large-scale theme parks in China, offering visitors a wide range of activities in which they can take part, instead of merely things to look at.
"There are not enough entertainment places in Shanghai," said Wang Naili, director of the city's tourism administration.

"People have two days off a week now. This is a good place with healthy entertainment for the family," he said. "Shanghai is a crossroads between east and west and people can see a U.S.-style culture here."
Admission costs 100 yuan ($12) for an adult and 80 yuan for a child or retirees, covering the costs of nearly all the rides.

"The price is too high," said one Shanghai resident watching the opening ceremony. "It will cost two parents with one child nearly 300 yuan just to get in, plus food and drink. Not many people can afford that."
